Managing students & batches

How do I manage chess students online?

Chess Nexus gives you a single coach dashboard to manage your whole roster — add students, group them into batches, set assignments, follow their progress and chat with them directly. It's free forever for up to 30 students. See the full coach guide for the step-by-step.

How do I organize students into chess batches?

Create batches on your Batches page and drop each student into one. Assignments, courses and class schedules can then target a whole batch at once instead of one student at a time — so running several groups stays simple even as your academy grows.

How do I manage multiple batches of students at once?

Everything you do — assignments, courses, class schedules, and private races and tournaments — can be aimed at a specific batch. Run several batches of different levels, set each batch's work once, and every student in it receives it.

Running classes

How do I run online chess classes?

Use the built-in live classroom — no Zoom needed. You get a shared board, video and audio, and can push a position or an endgame straight onto the board for the whole class. Every coach gets at least one live class a day free; paid plans raise the length, frequency and class size.

How do I structure lessons for beginners?

Build a course — an ordered syllabus of studies, master games, videos and free endgame positions — and enroll a beginner batch in it. Students work through it in sequence, and you can teach the same material live in the classroom. That keeps a beginner group on a clear path instead of ad-hoc lessons.

How do I create a chess curriculum?

A curriculum here is a course: an ordered list of lessons built from your own studies, master games, videos and endgame positions. Build it once, reuse it across batches, and students follow it lesson by lesson.

Homework & assignments

How do I assign homework to chess students?

Create an assignment and give it to a student or a whole batch. Assignments can be tactics drawn from a student's own blunders, Play-vs-Stockfish positions, or puzzle sets. Students receive it in their account and you see who's completed it — full detail in the coach guide.

How do I send chess homework automatically?

Save an assignment as a template and reuse it across students and batches instead of rebuilding it every week — you can also pull from a shared blunder library. That turns weekly homework into a couple of clicks. Assignments draw on the same tactics and puzzle engine students use, so the work is always relevant.

Tracking progress

How do I track my chess students' progress?

Each student has a progress view — puzzles solved, races and activity over time, plus games they've played on Lichess and Chess.com in the last 30 days. You can send parents a shareable progress report link so families see it too.

How do I analyze my student's games?

Students analyze their own games in the browser with a built-in engine, and you can turn a student's blunders into a tactics assignment — so they re-solve the exact positions they got wrong in real games. It's the fastest way to fix recurring mistakes. See how improvement is structured here.

Automating & growing

How do I reduce admin work in my chess academy?

Batches, assignment templates, reusable courses, a class schedule that notifies students automatically, and parent progress reports each remove a piece of manual work. Set things up once at the batch level and the platform delivers it to every student for you — that's the point of a coach-run platform over spreadsheets and chat apps.

How do I keep students engaged and motivated?

Private races and tournaments just for your students, puzzle challenges, a monthly focus theme, and visible progress all give students a reason to keep coming back. Friendly competition inside their own batch is often the strongest motivator for kids.

How do I start a chess academy online?

Sign up as a coach — free forever for up to 30 students, no card — add your students, group them into batches, build a course as your curriculum, and set a weekly class schedule. Everything an academy needs — roster, lessons, homework, live classes, reports — is in one place. You can even earn credit by referring other coaches.
